s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with peritonism and sepsis
salient_findings: Multi-organ involvement with lymphadenopathy and pulmonary consolidation
key_facts: 60-year-old man with history of heavy cigarette smoking
History of emphysema, hypertension, and prostate cancer in remission
4-hour history of acute right lower-quadrant abdominal pain
Fever of 38.5°C on admission
Hypotension with systolic blood pressure 90 mmHg
Tachycardia with heart rate 110/min
Peritonism in the right lower quadrant
Perforated appendix with collection and surrounding fat stranding on CT
Innumerable hepatic nodules and lymphadenopathy on CT
Pulmonary consolidation and collapse in the right lower lobe
Subtotal colectomy with end ileostomy performed
Postoperative ventilation required
Extubation attempt on day 3 failed

shortlist.label: Acute appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: Perforated appendix with collection and surrounding fat stranding on CT

shortlist.label: Sigmoid colon cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Thickened, woody sigmoid colon found during exploratory laparotomy

shortlist.label: Peritonitis
shortlist.why_kept: Peritonism in the right lower quadrant and purulent contamination during surgery

shortlist.label: Sepsis
shortlist.why_kept: Fever, hypotension, and tachycardia on admission

shortlist.label: Colorectal cancer with appendiceal metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: Innumerable hepatic nodules, lymphadenopathy, and thickened sigmoid colon

raw.rationale: The patient presented with fever, hypotension, tachycardia, and peritonism, which are all signs of sepsis, and the presence of a perforated appendix with purulent contamination and multi-organ involvement supports this diagnosis

rejected.label: Acute appendicitis
rejected.why: While the patient had a perforated appendix, this is a contributing factor to the sepsis rather than the primary diagnosis

rejected.label: Sigmoid colon cancer
rejected.why: Although the patient had a thickened sigmoid colon, the primary issue was the perforated appendix and subsequent sepsis

rejected.label: Peritonitis
rejected.why: Peritonitis is a symptom of the sepsis rather than the primary diagnosis

rejected.label: Colorectal cancer with appendiceal metastasis
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of appendiceal metastasis, and the primary issue was the perforated appendix and subsequent sepsis
